sources.title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Row Security Policies
sources.content: The PostgreSQL row-security documentation is the canonical row-level filtering (RLS) reference: policies apply per-role predicates at query time inside the database. It makes the layer question explicit for QA3: a query-time row filter is only as strong as every consumer path that reads rows, so caches and projections above the filter must apply the same policy predicates - a cache keyed without the scope/tenant attribute can serve rows the filter would deny. claims.text: [architecture_tradeoff] Decision (QA3) for the in-scope MVP profiles A and B: the retrieval isolation contract is per-scope indexing - a scope-addressed retrieval index over canonical scope-tagged rows - with the retrieval-time scope check retained as mandatory defense in depth, a cache key that binds (scope_id, object_id, version), scope-first projection, explicit residual risk, and a recorded migration trigger; shared-RLS is retained only as the SQL-level defense-in-depth baseline, never as the sole boundary; profile C is deferred.

[security_invariant] A query carrying a valid object id from a caller in another scope returns deny/empty with error detail byte-identical to the unknown-id denial and p50 latency within the documented local bound of the unknown-id baseline in the executed fixture matrix - no existence is revealed through timing or error detail.

[security_invariant] The executed fixture matrix reports 0 unauthorized content disclosures across all isolation, caching, and revocation cases (6 isolation cases + 6 cache/revocation cases over 3 scopes), and cross-scope projections are empty.

[security_invariant] A shared-index cache hit for a revoked or moved object never returns stale content to the old scope under the implemented contract: the cache key binds (scope_id, object_id, version) and revocation/transfer bump the version and remove the scope index entry, while the near-miss object-id-only shared cache is demonstrated to serve the stale entry and is rejected by the QA3 contract.

[security_invariant] The real AgentOS implementation scopes memory by scope_goal_id at the data model, SQL, and gateway layers: memory_read raises MemoryScopeViolation on cross-goal reads, the SQL WHERE scope_goal_id filter returns zero rows for another scope, and same-scope reads return the record with its scope/provenance fields intact.

[architecture_tradeoff] Per-scope indexing is strictly safer for the isolation property: a scope-addressed index makes a cross-scope hit structurally impossible and gives a small, attestable test surface, whereas a shared index with row-level retrieval filtering is cheaper to build but cannot by itself prove absence of leakage because any consumer path above the filter - notably a shared cache and error/timing behavior - must independently re-apply the scope predicate.

[architecture_tradeoff] Per-scope indexing is sufficiently useful at the MVP envelope: index maintenance cost is linear in the number of scopes, the in-scope profiles run single-process on one store per the QA1 decision, and the SRC-06 volume envelope (planning estimates) keeps per-scope index size and write amplification in-process and bounded.

[scope_fact] A scope identifier is the unit of retrieval isolation: storage binds every record to a scope_goal_id, the audit shapes treat workspace scope as non-transitive (ownership in another workspace does not become valid through a link), and the QA3 contract uses canonical scope labels (scope-alpha, scope-beta, scope-gamma) as tenants of the isolation fixtures.

[scope_fact] Projection applies scope filtering before materializing any content: every same-scope retrieved record retains scope_id and provenance fields, and every cross-scope projection is empty - scope and provenance survive projection exactly when the caller's scope matches the record scope.

[test_measurement] Probe cross-scope-isolation executed and passed 6 isolation cases over 3 scopes (same-scope positive control; cross-scope deny with identical error detail and bounded timing; shared-RLS boundary with near-miss shared-cache demonstration; revoked-object; moved-object scope transfer; projection survival), plus a real-gateway memory-scoping check; p50 delta between cross-scope and unknown-id denial was within the documented 5 ms local bound with error-detail equality.

[test_measurement] Probe cache-revocation executed and passed 6 cache/revocation cases over 3 scopes with an injectable clock (revoke vs warm cache; move vs warm cache; edit version bump; revoked owner-scope deny; TTL expiry; invalidation cascade) reporting 0 stale servings by the implemented cache and 0 unauthorized disclosures, while the near-miss object-id-only shared-cache staleness hazard is recorded as observed data.

[test_measurement] The probes drove the real ToolGateway memory path against a fresh agentos.db: cross-goal memory_read raised MemoryScopeViolation, the SQL scope_goal_id filter returned zero cross-scope rows, same-scope read returned the record, and memory_record carried scope_goal_id per the data model.

[residual_risk] The timing uniformity observation (identical error detail plus bounded p50 delta) is a deterministic in-process measurement over warm samples, not a constant-time proof; under OS scheduler load, a remote, multi-process, or production deployment could observe different jitter, so the hard acceptance remains the identical deny semantics and the error-detail equality, with timing asserted only to a generous local bound.

[residual_risk] Residual risks remain: cache TTL/eviction and any admin/indexer bypass path must re-apply the same scope predicates; revocation latency at <=5 s is not proven here (S1-008 domain); and profile-C MLS/TEE isolation evidence is weak per G-04 and is deferred to S1-018 with a conditional rollout posture - none of these are claimed closed by this ticket.

[decision] Migration trigger: reconsider the QA3 contract when (a) measured multi-tenant growth drives per-scope index maintenance beyond the in-process envelope, (b) a shared or federated index with proven policy-attribute cache keys is required by a production search service, or (c) profile-C rollout reaches a deployment decision (S1-018) that changes the isolation boundary - each requiring new measured evidence and a fresh trust-boundary review.

[decision] Non-goals for this decision: no production search service is built, no ranking quality claim is made, and no profile-C rollout is performed by this ticket; the decision boundary is the retrieval isolation contract for the in-scope profiles only.

research_plan.content:
# Question
QA3: is per-scope indexing safer and sufficiently useful than a shared index with row-level retrieval filtering, and can either design prove no cross-scope reads or leakage?

# Method
Offline, stdlib-only experimental study. (1) Freeze the current isolation evidence: spec/SPEC.md memory scoping, gateway.py memory_read, migration 0001 memory_record, AGENTS.md invariants, S1-003 scope/provenance shapes, and the QA3 question from SRC-03 (all hash-bound in the source registry). (2) Run the deterministic retrieval_isolation_probe.py against the recorded QA3 decision contract (agentos.s1-007-qa3-contract/v1): 3 scopes (scope-alpha, scope-beta, scope-gamma) and 6 isolation cases, including cross-scope query timing and error-detail uniformity (valid object id from another scope must deny exactly like an unknown id), shared-RLS boundary with the near-miss shared-cache demonstration, revoked-object and moved-object cases, and provenance survival through projection, PLUS 6 cache/revocation cases with an injectable clock and a real-gateway memory-scoping check. (3) Assert the quantitative acceptance: >=3 scopes, >=6 cases, 0 unauthorized content disclosures, both probes pass, and scope/provenance fields survive projection.

# Source mix
All four required evidence classes are present: ontology/scope (SRC-05, S1-003-SHAPES, AGENTS-INVARIANTS), architecture/data model (SPEC-ARCH, GATEWAY-IMPL, MIGRATIONS-IMPL, S1-003-BUNDLE, S1-005-BUNDLE, SRC-03, SRC-06, PLAN-DEF), authorization/security (SRC-02, SRC-07, OWASP-AUTHZ, PG-RLS), and retrieval isolation test method (OWASP-WSTG-IDOR plus the local S1-007-RESULTS execution artifact).

# Scope
Scope identifiers, per-scope versus shared index, retrieval-time policy checks, RLS/projection boundaries, provenance and cache behavior, and cross-tenant adversarial tests for the in-scope profiles.

# Non-scope
Production search service, ranking quality optimization, profile-C rollout, and any measured reliability claim for a deployed multi-tenant service.

# Stop rule
Escalate on any cross-scope disclosure, unverifiable cache invalidation, or a requirement for admin-blind indexing that conflicts with the documented profile-C boundary; the ticket fails closed if any probe does not reach its expected verdict.

architecture_models.content:
# Retrieval isolation architecture (as designed for the in-scope profiles)
Canonical scope-tagged rows (memory_record.scope_goal_id and future knowledge-store rows) -> per-scope retrieval index (scope-addressed, one entry per object per scope) -> mandatory retrieval-time scope/status check -> scope+version cache -> scope-first projection. The existing SQL scope filter (SPEC.md 7) stays as the storage-level defense in depth. The per-scope index is a retrieval projection layer inside one process/one store (QA1 monolith decision), not a distributed search service.

mental_model.content:
# Mental model
Isolation is a property of the retrieval PATH, not of the storage table. A scope-tagged row is safe only while every path that can materialize it re-applies the scope predicate. A per-scope index makes the safe path the only path: the index itself is scope-addressed, so a cross-scope lookup cannot even reach the row. A shared index with row-level filtering moves the predicate into every consumer (query, cache, projection, error text, timing), and each of those is a separate place to leak.

# Where intuition misleads
'Row-level security' sounds like a complete boundary, but the row filter is only the bottom layer: a cache above it that keys by object id alone, or a deny path whose error text differs for known ids, leaks existence and stale content. The QA3 contract treats the SQL scope filter as defense in depth, never as the sole boundary.

# Scope identity
A scope identifier names the tenant of a record (goal-scoped today via scope_goal_id). Scope is non-transitive: a record's presence in a graph or an index under one scope does not make it retrievable under another scope.

# Proof posture
What can be proven is fail-closed behavior on the implemented path (identical deny semantics, scope+version cache keys, version-bumped invalidation, scope-first projection) plus a bounded local timing observation; constant-time guarantees for arbitrary deployments are not claimed.

ontology.content:
# Terms
- scope_identifier: the unit of retrieval isolation; stored as scope_goal_id today, canonically expressed as tenant:goal in the QA3 contract fixtures (scope-alpha, scope-beta, scope-gamma).
- per_scope_index: a retrieval index addressed by scope; an object is reachable only through its own scope's index entry.
- shared_rls: row-level retrieval filtering (WHERE scope scope_id = ?) over a shared table/index; the storage-level baseline that must not be the sole boundary.
- retrieval_time_policy_check: the mandatory scope+status verification run on every query path, including cache hits.
- scope_first_projection: projecting an object by applying the scope predicate before materializing any content field.
- provenance_fields: the scope, author, and canonical_source identity carried with a record (S1-003 shapes); survivors of projection for same-scope records only.
- cache_key: must bind (scope_id, object_id, version); scopeless or object-id-only keys are a rejected near miss.
- revocation_bump: a version increment plus index-entry removal applied on revoke/move/supersede so all cached keys die.
- profile: an isolation posture class (A, B in scope here; C deferred to S1-018).

mathematical_model.content:
# Sets and predicates
Let O be canonical objects with scope s(o) in {scope-alpha, scope-beta, scope-gamma}, version v(o), status st(o) in {active, revoked}, and provenance p(o). Let I(x) be the per-scope index of scope x, and C(s,id,v) the cache with key (scope, id, version).

Retrieved(s_c, q):= exists o in O : q.id = o.id AND o in I(s_c) AND st(o)=active AND moved(o) is null.
Deny(s_c, q):= not Retrieved(...). For q.id in O with s(q.id) != s_c, Deny detail equals the unknown-id detail: err(q) = "no_such_object" in both cases (indistinguishability predicate).
Disclosure := |{r : r.content visible to s_c where s(r) != s_c}|. Acceptance: Disclosure = 0.
Stale(s_c, q):= served content with version < v(o) after any revoke/move/edit of o. Cache invalidation is by construction: revoke/move/edit bump v(o) and remove I(x) entries, so key (s_c, q.id, v_old) can never be produced again.
Timing: t_D(q_known_cross) vs t_D(q_unknown); measured p50 delta over 120 warm samples, asserted <= 5 ms with per-query cap 50 ms (bounded local observation, not constant-time proof).
Projection P(r) := scope-first filter then fields (scope_id, provenance, content); P(cross-scope) = empty set.

# Measurements
6 isolation cases + 6 cache/revocation cases (12 total) over 3 scopes, all expected outcomes matched; unauthorized_disclosures = 0; stale_servings = 0; error-detail equality = true; near-miss shared-cache hazard observed as data and rejected by the contract; real gateway cross-goal read denied (MemoryScopeViolation) with 0 cross-scope SQL rows.

# Boundary
These predicates are an executable oracle for the in-process contract, not a proof of production multi-tenant behavior, network-level constant time, or profile-C MLS/TEE isolation.

synthesis_and_gaps.content:
# Result
QA3 resolved for the in-scope profiles: per-scope indexing over the shared-RLS baseline. 12 executable cases (6 isolation + 6 cache/revocation) over 3 scopes passed with 0 unauthorized disclosures and 0 stale cache servings; both adversarial probes pass; the real gateway memory scoping path is exercised and denies cross-goal reads. The QA3 decision contract records policy, threat model, test boundary, residual risk, migration triggers and non-goals.

# What is ready
S1-008 may consume the version-bumped invalidation contract for revocation; S1-016 may consume the scope-identifier semantics; S1-018 and S1-019 may consume the QA3 selection and the profile-C deferral. The SQL scope filter plus gateway MemoryScopeViolation remain canonical MVP enforcement; the per-scope index is the retrieval projection layer selected here.

# Open gaps
No production multi-tenant deployment or network-level timing was measured. Constant-time behavior is not claimed; revocation latency <=5 s and profile-C MLS/TEE isolation remain open (S1-008, S1-018). Ranking quality and a production search service are out of scope.

# Recommendation
Adopt per-scope indexing for the in-scope profiles with the recorded contract; revisit via the migration triggers with new measured evidence and a fresh trust-boundary review.

independent_audit.content:

(3) Adversarial near-miss rejection: the shared-RLS-as-sole-design and object-id-only cache-key variants are rejected by the contract and their leak is demonstrated as data in the simulation (never used by the implemented path). (4) Probes pass with 0 disclosures and 0 stale servings, and the real gateway memory-scoping path denies cross-goal reads. (5) Platform plan states the chosen contract.

# Limits
The isolation evidence is a deterministic in-process simulation plus the real single-process gateway path; it is not a production or multi-host measurement. Timing uniformity is a bounded local observation, not a constant-time proof. External campaign sources (SRC-02/03/05/06/07) were verified by preserved-campaign identity and prior documented review/hashes offline, not re-fetched. Producer and verifier are process-separated roles in one local environment, not independent human operators. Profile-C MLS/TEE isolation and production revocation latency remain out of scope.

pass_with_limits - the QA3 decision is supported at design confidence for the in-scope profiles; production and profile-C evidence remain open items, not byproducts of this ticket.

platform_plan.content:
# Scope
Adopt the QA3 retrieval-isolation contract for the in-scope profiles (A, B): per-scope indexing as the primary retrieval boundary over canonical scope-tagged rows, with the retrieval-time scope check mandatory (defense in depth), cache keys binding (scope_id, object_id, version), and scope-first projection. The existing SQL scope filter (SPEC.md 7) and gateway MemoryScopeViolation remain canonical MVP enforcement. This plan builds no production search service, makes no ranking quality claim, and performs no profile-C rollout.

# Architecture
Single-process modular monolith per QA1 (S1-005): one store, gateway-only effects, atomic transition+audit. Retrieval adds a scope-addressed index layer over the same store: per-scope index entries keyed (scope_id, object_id) with entry version; scope+version cache; a single deny path where 'unknown id' and 'valid id in another scope' are byte-identical; version-bumped invalidation on revoke/move/edit; scope-first projection that preserves scope_id and provenance for same-scope records and yields empty for cross-scope calls. Every cache-hit path still runs the retrieval-time scope check.

# Workstreams
1. Freeze this bundle's QA3 contract and bind S1-008 (revocation), S1-016 (scope lineage) and S1-019 (synthesis) to it. 2. Add the per-scope retrieval index and scope+version cache to the context-compiler retrieval path behind the existing gateway scope checks. 3. Wire retrieval_isolation_probe.py into the ticket probes and re-run on any retrieval-path change. 4. Record migration triggers in the runbook: multi-tenant growth, shared/federated index requirement, profile-C deployment decision. 5. Keep the near-miss library (shared-RLS-sole, object-id-only cache keys) as regression fixtures so the rejected designs cannot reappear silently.

# Milestones
M1: QA3 decision recorded with passing probes (this ticket). M2: S1-008 consumes the version-bumped invalidation contract. M3: per-scope index + scope+version cache landed on the retrieval path and regression probes green. M4: first measured multi-scope load observation before any shared/federated index re-evaluation.

# Verification
Require: both probes pass with 0 unauthorized disclosures and 0 stale cache servings; >=3 scopes and >=6 isolation cases in the fixture set; error-detail equality between cross-scope and unknown-id denials with bounded p50 delta; scope_id and provenance fields survive projection for same-scope records; real gateway cross-goal read raises MemoryScopeViolation; repo-local source hashes verified from disk; and an independent reviewer reproduces the research-plan command.

# Risks
Timing uniformity is a bounded local observation, not a constant-time proof; cache TTL/eviction and admin or indexer bypass paths must re-apply the same scope predicates; revocation latency <=5 s remains S1-008 evidence; profile-C MLS/TEE isolation evidence is weak (G-04) and rollout stays deferred to S1-018; the plan adds retrieval-layer complexity that must not diverge from the QA1 single-writer/atomic-audit invariants.

# Open decisions
Choose the exact per-scope index representation (SQL index rows vs sidecar partition) when the retrieval path is implemented; decide cache sizing/TTL policy from measured hit rates; decide whether the shared-RLS SQL filter remains a scanned defense-in-depth path or gains its own (scope_goal_id, id) index; confirm whether S1-016 scope/lineage semantics change the scope-identifier encoding before profile-B rollouts.
